result.title: Spatial Harness: Grounding Spatial Reasoning in Executable World States with Physics Engines
result.summary: Spatial reasoning requires understanding how objects and observers are arranged in a scene and how their relations change with viewpoint or movement. Vision-language models (VLMs) typically perform both steps through model-internal reasoning, forming an implicit scene interpretation from partial views and imagining the consequences of spatial transformations. A misread scene can lead to a wrong answer, while even a correct interpretation does not ensure that imagined transformations satisfy spatial constraints. We introduce Spatial Harness, which represents scenes as explicit and executable world states to ground spatial reasoning in physics-engine feedback. A Perceiver integrates scene constraints extracted from the question with specialized visual estimates to place objects and cameras in a shared coordinate frame. The resulting state is instantiated in a physics engine, where a Reasoner executes viewpoint changes and uses computed measurements and rendered views to guide reasoning. We evaluate on MindCube, SAT, MMSI-Bench, and SpatialRGPT-Bench with open- and closed-weight VLMs. On MindCube, Spatial Harness improves Qwen3.5-27B from 52.70% to 71.14%, surpassing pySpatial by 7.52 percentage points. Given identical annotated object and camera poses, it reaches 98.25% versus 71.81% for model-internal reasoning. Code is publicly available at: https://github.com/tmlr-group/Spatial-Harness

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Spatial Harness，将场景显式表示为可执行世界状态：用 Perceiver 结合问题约束与视觉估计放置物体和相机，再由物理引擎执行视角变换并生成测量与渲染视图来引导 VLM 空间推理。
AI.relevance_reason: 可作为「显式外部世界状态」与 LVR 隐式场景表征的直接对照，涉及几何信息保留、视角变换证据获取及物理引擎计算成本；其外部状态是否真正替代模型内部推理、以及感知误差如何传导，仍待核查。
